slides.title: Past simple vs present perfect

rows.label: FORM
rows.left:
V2 / past form
She lost her keys.
rows.right:
have / has + V3 (past participle)
She has lost her keys.

rows.label: MEANING
rows.left: A finished event at a finished time.
rows.right: A past event with a result or relevance now.

rows.label: USE
rows.left: Stories, dates, sequences: yesterday, in 2019, then.
rows.right: Experience, change, unfinished: ever, since, so far.

slides.trap:
Finished time: “I have seen him yesterday.” ✗ → “I saw him yesterday.” ✓
Unfinished time: “I saw him since 2019.” ✗ → “I have seen him since 2019.” ✓
slides.notes: 先用两个时间轴对比过去时和现在完成时。

slides.title: Question analysis: “just passing by”
slides.stem: What does the writer suggest by saying that people “usually mean they are stopping for a while”?

options.text: The kiosk has become a place people visit on purpose.
People no longer buy newspapers at the kiosk.
The street has become busier than before.
The writer dislikes people who pass by.

slides.evidence: “But now, when people say they are ‘just passing by,’ they usually mean they are stopping for a while.”
slides.why: The phrase usually means “not staying.” The ending reverses it: passing by now leads to stopping.
slides.trap: B is true but does not answer the question. D invents an attitude the writer never shows.
slides.pattern: PATTERN · Locate the phrase → compare its usual meaning with the ending → infer what the reversal says about the place.
slides.notes: 先做题，不要看答案；圈出时间状语。
